periods.title: City Walls Walk
periods.text: Begin with the city walls, Dubrovnik's defining experience. The complete circuit is 2km around the top of the fortifications, with views plunging down into the terracotta rooftops of the Old Town on one side and the deep blue Adriatic on the other. The walls are up to 25m high and 6m thick, with towers, bastions, and fortresses along the route. The Minčeta Tower at the highest point offers a 360-degree panorama. Allow 90 minutes for the full circuit, stopping to photograph the Lovrijenac fortress, the harbour, and the island of Lokrum.
periods.tip: Enter the walls from the Pile Gate entrance at 8am when they open. By 10am the circuit is packed with cruise-ship visitors. The morning light from the east illuminates the Old Town beautifully.

periods.title: Old Town Exploration
periods.text: Descend into the Old Town and walk the Stradun, the polished limestone main street running from the Pile Gate to the Old Port. Visit the Rector's Palace (now a museum), the Franciscan Monastery with Europe's third-oldest pharmacy, and the Cathedral of the Assumption. Wander the side streets, where narrow lanes climb steeply from the Stradun to the walls, with laundry lines, potted plants, and cats sunning on stone steps. The contrast between the grand Stradun and the intimate residential lanes is one of Dubrovnik's greatest charms.
periods.tip: The Dubrovnik Card covers most attractions and the walls. Buy the 1-day or 3-day version online for significant savings over individual tickets.

periods.title: Buža Bar & Sunset
periods.text: Find Buža Bar, a hidden cliff bar accessed through a hole in the city walls on the south side of the Old Town. There is no sign; look for the small doorway marked "Cold Drinks" near the Jesuit Church. Step through and you are on a series of rock terraces perched above the open Adriatic with nothing between you and the horizon. Order a beer or cocktail, watch cliff-jumpers launch into the deep blue water below, and stay for the sunset. This is one of the most extraordinary bar locations in the world.
periods.tip: Buža gets crowded by late afternoon, so arrive by 5pm for a good terrace spot. Bring cash; cards may not be accepted. There are two Buža bars, and Buža 2 is the more famous one.

3.title: City Walls, Old Town & Buža Bar

periods.title: City Walls Circuit
periods.text: Walk the full 2km city walls circuit starting from the Pile Gate entrance at opening time. The route passes the Minčeta Tower (highest point with the best panorama), the Revelin Fortress, the harbour-side walls, and the Bokar Fortress above the sea. Views alternate between the terracotta rooftops of the Old Town and the deep Adriatic. The walls were never breached in their 800-year history and remain one of the finest fortification systems in Europe.
periods.tip: Start at 8am sharp, because by 10am the walls are crowded with cruise passengers. Bring water, sunscreen, and a hat, as the circuit is fully exposed with no shade.

periods.title: Old Town Deep Dive
periods.text: Walk the Stradun and explore the side streets. Visit the Rector's Palace for Dubrovnik's history as an independent republic, the Franciscan Monastery with its 14th-century pharmacy, and the War Photo Limited gallery, a powerful exhibition of conflict photography. Climb the steep lanes to the Jesuit Stairs (a Game of Thrones filming location) and the Church of St. Ignatius for views over the rooftops.
periods.tip: The Dubrovnik Card includes walls, museums, and transport. The 1 or 3-day version saves significantly over buying individual tickets.

periods.title: Buža Bar Sunset & Old Port Dinner
periods.text: Find the hidden Buža Bar through the unmarked hole in the south wall, where rock terraces sit above the open Adriatic with cliff-jumping and sunset views. After sunset, walk to the Old Port for dinner at one of the harbour-side restaurants. Fresh Adriatic fish, octopus salad, and local Pelješac wine (Dingač or Postup) are the highlights of Dubrovnik dining.
periods.tip: Arrive at Buža by 5pm for a terrace seat. For dinner, avoid the Stradun tourist traps. The harbour restaurants and the lanes behind the Cathedral are better value.

periods.title: Ferry to Lokrum Island
periods.text: Take the 15-minute ferry from the Old Port to Lokrum, an uninhabited island nature reserve 600m offshore. The island is a Mediterranean botanical garden with century-old pine and cypress forests, a ruined Benedictine monastery, a saltwater lake (the Dead Sea) for swimming, and peacocks wandering the paths. The rocky coastline has excellent snorkelling in crystal-clear water. The monastery ruins include the location of the Iron Throne from Game of Thrones.
periods.tip: Ferries run every 30 minutes from the Old Port. Bring snacks and water, as the island has a café but it is limited and pricey. No overnight stays are permitted.

periods.title: Cable Car to Srđ
periods.text: Return to the mainland and take the cable car to the summit of Mount Srđ (412m), the most comprehensive viewpoint of Dubrovnik. The entire walled city, the harbour, Lokrum island, the Elafiti archipelago, and the coastline stretching south to Montenegro are laid out below. The Fort Imperial at the summit houses a museum of the 1991 siege, when the city was shelled for months during the Croatian War of Independence, a powerful and sobering counterpoint to the beauty below.
periods.tip: Take the cable car up and walk down. The zigzag path takes about 45 minutes and offers changing perspectives of the city. Or vice versa to save energy.

periods.title: Kayaking & Sunset
periods.text: Join a sunset sea kayaking tour from the Pile Gate beach. Paddle along the base of the city walls, around the Bokar and Lovrijenac fortresses, and across to Lokrum, seeing Dubrovnik from sea level as ancient mariners would have. The walls reflected in the calm evening water, lit by the setting sun, is one of the most photogenic perspectives of the city.
periods.tip: Book the sunset kayak tour at least a day ahead, as it is the most popular activity in Dubrovnik. No experience required; guides provide instruction.

periods.title: Elafiti Islands Boat Trip
periods.text: Take a day-trip boat to the Elafiti Islands, a car-free archipelago northwest of Dubrovnik. The three main islands (Koločep, Lopud, and Šipan) are connected by a hop-on-hop-off ferry. Koločep has forest walking trails and secluded swimming coves. Lopud's Šunj Beach is a rare sandy beach on the Adriatic with shallow, warm water and a beach bar. Šipan is the largest with olive groves, vineyards, and quiet village harbours.
periods.tip: The regular Jadrolinija ferry to the Elafiti is much cheaper than organised tours. Take the earliest ferry and island-hop through the day.

periods.title: Šunj Beach & Island Swimming
periods.text: Spend the afternoon on Lopud's Šunj Beach, a crescent of sand in a sheltered bay with clear turquoise water. The 15-minute walk from the Lopud ferry dock crosses the island through olive groves and Mediterranean gardens. Swim, sunbathe, and eat at the simple beach restaurant. This is one of the most beautiful beaches accessible from Dubrovnik.
periods.tip: Bring a towel and picnic supplies, as the beach restaurant is the only option and prices reflect the captive audience. The walk is flat and shaded.

periods.title: Farewell Stradun Walk & Dinner
periods.text: Return by ferry and walk the Stradun one final time as the evening light turns the limestone golden. The Old Town empties after the cruise ships depart and becomes dramatically more peaceful. Eat a farewell dinner of grilled fish and Pelješac wine at a quiet lane restaurant, then sit at the harbour wall and watch the boats in the Old Port.
periods.tip: The Old Town is most magical after 7pm when day-trippers leave, as the atmosphere transforms completely. Book a late dinner for the best experience.

periods.title: City Walls Circuit
periods.text: Walk the 2km walls at opening time. The Minčeta Tower, Revelin Fortress, and Bokar Fortress punctuate the route with the Old Town rooftops and Adriatic alternating below. Allow 90 minutes for the full circuit with photo stops.
periods.tip: Enter at 8am from Pile Gate, because by 10am cruise groups flood the walls. Bring water, sunscreen, and a hat.

periods.title: Stradun & Museums
periods.text: Explore the Old Town: Rector's Palace, Franciscan Monastery pharmacy, Cathedral of the Assumption, and the steep residential lanes. War Photo Limited gallery is a powerful exhibition of conflict photography worth an hour.
periods.tip: Buy a Dubrovnik Card for walls, museums, and transport, a significant saving over individual tickets.

periods.title: Buža Bar Sunset
periods.text: Find Buža Bar through the unmarked hole in the south wall, where cliff terraces sit above the open sea with sunset views. After dark, walk to the Old Port for harbour-side dinner with Pelješac wine.
periods.tip: Arrive by 5pm. Bring cash, as cards may not work. Look for the "Cold Drinks" doorway near the Jesuit Church.

periods.title: Lokrum Nature Reserve
periods.text: Ferry to Lokrum island (15 minutes), an uninhabited reserve with pine forests, a Benedictine monastery ruin, peacocks, and the saltwater Dead Sea lake. Swim in the crystal-clear water at rocky coves along the south coast. Explore the botanical gardens planted by Archduke Maximilian in the 19th century.
periods.tip: Ferries run every 30 minutes. Bring snacks and water, as island facilities are limited.

periods.title: Snorkelling & Dead Sea
periods.text: Swim in the Dead Sea, a saltwater lake in the island's interior connected to the ocean by an underwater channel. The water is warmer and calmer than the open sea. Snorkel along the south coast for the clearest water and most marine life.
periods.tip: Bring a mask and snorkel, as the underwater visibility is exceptional. Water shoes help on the rocky entries.

periods.title: Old Port Seafood Dinner
periods.text: Return by ferry and eat at the Old Port: grilled catch of the day, black risotto, or octopus peka. The harbour restaurants are at their best in the evening when the fortress walls are illuminated.
periods.tip: Skip the Stradun restaurants. The lanes behind the Cathedral and the harbour have better food at lower prices.

periods.title: Mount Srđ & Fort Imperial
periods.text: Cable car to Mount Srđ (412m) for the definitive Dubrovnik panorama. The Fort Imperial museum tells the story of the 1991 siege, when shells rained on the city for months. The exhibit is sobering and essential context for understanding modern Dubrovnik.
periods.tip: Take the cable car up and walk down the zigzag path (45 minutes) for changing perspectives. Or hike up and ride down.

periods.title: Game of Thrones Walking Tour
periods.text: Explore the city through the lens of its most famous filming locations: the Jesuit Stairs (Walk of Shame), Lovrijenac Fortress (Red Keep), Minčeta Tower (House of the Undying), and Trsteno Arboretum gardens (Tyrell Gardens, a short bus ride). Whether or not you are a fan, the locations reveal parts of the city you might otherwise miss.
periods.tip: Self-guided tours with online maps are free. Paid tours add context but are not necessary. Lovrijenac Fortress is included in the Dubrovnik Card.

periods.title: Sunset Sea Kayaking
periods.text: Paddle along the base of the city walls at sunset for the most spectacular perspective of Dubrovnik. The walls reflected in calm evening water, the Lovrijenac fortress silhouetted against the sky, and the harbour lights coming on as you return. No kayaking experience is needed.
periods.tip: Book at least a day ahead, as the sunset tour is the most popular activity in Dubrovnik. Tours depart from Pile Gate beach.

periods.title: Ferry to Koločep & Lopud
periods.text: Take the morning ferry to the Elafiti Islands, car-free and pine-forested islands northwest of Dubrovnik. Start at Koločep for forest trails and secluded swimming coves, then hop to Lopud on the next ferry.
periods.tip: Use the regular Jadrolinija ferry, much cheaper than organised day trips. Check the schedule and plan your island-hopping accordingly.

periods.title: Šunj Beach on Lopud
periods.text: Walk 15 minutes across Lopud to Šunj Beach, a sandy crescent in a sheltered bay with turquoise water. One of the few sandy beaches in the Dubrovnik area and utterly beautiful. Swim, sunbathe, and eat at the simple beach restaurant.
periods.tip: Bring supplies, as the beach restaurant is the only option and charges premium prices.

periods.title: Lopud Harbour Dinner
periods.text: Eat at a harbour-side restaurant on Lopud before taking the evening ferry back to Dubrovnik. The island pace of life, with no cars and no rush, is a wonderful contrast to the crowds of the Old Town.
periods.tip: Check the last ferry time carefully. Lopud harbour restaurants serve excellent fresh fish at slightly lower prices than Dubrovnik.

periods.title: Drive to Pelješac
periods.text: Rent a car or join a tour to the Pelješac Peninsula, a long mountainous finger of land famous for Croatia's best red wine. The drive north along the coast passes the town of Ston with its 5km medieval walls (the second-longest fortification in the world after the Great Wall) and salt pans that have operated since Roman times. Walk a section of the Ston walls before continuing.
periods.tip: Ston is famous for oysters farmed in the bay, so stop for a dozen fresh oysters at a harbour restaurant. They cost a fraction of what you would pay in Dubrovnik.

periods.title: Dingač Wine Tasting
periods.text: Continue to the Dingač wine region, Croatia's first protected wine designation, where Plavac Mali grapes grow on impossibly steep south-facing slopes above the Adriatic. Visit a family winery (Matuško, Bura, or Kiridžija) for a tasting of Dingač and Postup wines, powerful, full-bodied reds with character that rivals their more famous Mediterranean counterparts. The vineyards themselves, clinging to near-vertical hillsides above the sea, are an extraordinary sight.
periods.tip: Book winery visits ahead, as many are family operations and need advance notice. Tastings typically cost 10–20 euros and include 4–6 wines with local cheese and ham.

periods.title: Return via Trsteno
periods.text: Drive back via Trsteno and visit the Trsteno Arboretum, a Renaissance garden with ancient plane trees, aqueducts, and Mediterranean plant collections overlooking the sea. This was the Tyrell Gardens in Game of Thrones. Return to Dubrovnik for a late dinner.
periods.tip: Trsteno is 20km northwest of Dubrovnik and closes around 7pm, so plan your return timing accordingly.

periods.title: Drive to Kotor
periods.text: Cross the border into Montenegro (2 hours) and drive around the Bay of Kotor, the southernmost fjord in Europe. The road follows the water past small fishing villages, medieval churches, and the town of Perast with its two tiny islands. The scenery is extraordinary, with mountains rising vertically from the still, dark water of the inner bay.
periods.tip: Bring your passport, as Montenegro is not in the EU. Border crossings can take 30–60 minutes in summer. Start early to avoid the worst queues.

periods.title: Kotor Old Town & Fortress
periods.text: Explore Kotor's medieval old town, compact, atmospheric, and ringed by massive walls. Climb the 1,350 steps to the San Giovanni fortress for one of the most dramatic viewpoints in the Balkans, with the entire bay laid out below and mountains on every side. The climb is steep and takes 60–90 minutes but the panorama justifies every step.
periods.tip: Start the fortress climb early and bring water, as there is no shade and the steps are exposed. The fortress entry fee is paid at the gate.

periods.title: Perast & Return
periods.text: Stop in Perast on the return, a tiny Baroque town on the bay with two island churches you can visit by taxi boat. Our Lady of the Rocks is an artificial island built by local fishermen over centuries of dropping rocks around a sacred painting. Eat fresh fish at a waterfront restaurant before driving back to Dubrovnik.
periods.tip: The taxi boat to Our Lady of the Rocks costs just a few euros and takes 5 minutes. The church interior and story are worth the quick trip.

periods.title: Banje Beach & Final Swim
periods.text: Spend your final morning at Banje Beach, the main beach east of the Old Town with views of the walls and Lokrum island. The water is clean and deep, the pebble beach has sun-lounger rentals, and the view of the fortress walls from the water is stunning. A final Adriatic swim to close out your Dubrovnik week.
periods.tip: Banje has a free public section and a paid beach club. The free section is just as good for swimming, with the same view.

periods.title: Gundulić Market & Souvenirs
periods.text: Visit the Gundulić Square morning market for lavender, honey, olive oil, and local liqueurs. Walk the Old Town lanes one final time and discover details you missed in the stonework, window boxes, and hidden courtyards. The side streets north of the Stradun are the least visited and the most atmospheric.
periods.tip: The Gundulić market is busiest before noon. Lavender sachets and Croatian olive oil make excellent lightweight souvenirs.

periods.title: Farewell Dinner & Departure
periods.text: End your week with dinner at the Old Port, watching the boats, the fortress lights, and the evening promenade from your table. Order a final glass of Dingač wine and grilled Adriatic fish. Dubrovnik airport is 20 minutes away; the bus station connects to Split, Montenegro, and beyond.
periods.tip: Book airport shuttles or buses in advance, as taxis from the Old Town to the airport are expensive. The airport bus is cheap and reliable.

budgetTips.title: Buy the Dubrovnik Card
budgetTips.text: The 1-day or 3-day Dubrovnik Card includes walls, museums, and bus transport, significantly cheaper than buying individual tickets. Buy online for an additional discount.

budgetTips.title: Eat outside the walls
budgetTips.text: Restaurants inside the Old Town charge a significant premium. Walk 5 minutes to Gruž harbour or Lapad for the same quality food at 30–40% lower prices.

budgetTips.title: Use public ferries
budgetTips.text: The Jadrolinija ferries to the Elafiti Islands and Lokrum are far cheaper than organised tour boats. Plan your own island-hopping with the public schedule.

budgetTips.title: Visit off-peak
budgetTips.text: May–June and September–October have warm weather, swimming conditions, and dramatically fewer cruise-ship crowds. July–August is peak season with higher prices and overwhelming crowds.

budgetTips.title: Walk the walls early
budgetTips.text: The walls are the main expense, so make the most of it by going at 8am opening when you have space to enjoy the views without the midday crush.

budgetTips.title: Bring your own snorkelling gear
budgetTips.text: Renting masks and snorkels on Lokrum is overpriced. Pack your own for unlimited free snorkelling at every rocky cove around Dubrovnik.

budgetBreakdown.notes: Outside walls → Old Town → fine dining
Public ferry → bus tours → private boat
Dubrovnik Card covers the main sites

practicalInfo.title: Entry & Visas
items: Croatia is in the Schengen Zone. EU/EEA citizens enter freely; others may need a visa or ETIAS
Keep digital and physical copies of your passport and travel insurance
Day trips to Montenegro require a passport, so check visa requirements for your nationality

practicalInfo.title: Health & Safety
items: Tap water is safe throughout Dubrovnik, so refill bottles at public fountains
Sun protection is essential, as the white limestone reflects intense heat. Carry water on the walls walk
The Old Town is very safe but crowded. Watch for pickpockets at the Pile Gate entrance and on the Stradun

practicalInfo.title: Getting Around
items: The Old Town is entirely pedestrian, so everything inside the walls is on foot
Local buses connect the Old Town to Gruž harbour, Lapad, and the airport cheaply and frequently
Ferries to Lokrum (15 min) and the Elafiti Islands depart from the Old Port and Gruž harbour

practicalInfo.title: Connectivity
items: Free WiFi at most cafés and accommodation. The Old Town has good coverage
EU roaming rules apply, so European SIMs work at no extra cost. Buy a local SIM at the airport for non-EU visitors
Mobile signal is reliable on the nearby islands and the Pelješac Peninsula

practicalInfo.title: Money
items: Currency: EUR (Euro) since 2023. Cards accepted widely; carry cash for market vendors and Buža Bar
ATMs are available inside and outside the walls. Avoid airport exchange with poor rates
Tipping: round up the bill or add 10% for good service. Not obligatory but appreciated

practicalInfo.title: Packing Tips
items: Comfortable shoes with grip, as the limestone streets are polished smooth and slippery when wet
Swimsuit, reef shoes, and snorkelling gear, as the rocky coastline has clear water at every turn
A hat and reusable water bottle are essential for the walls walk and Srđ climb

culturalTips.title: Respect the History
culturalTips.text: Dubrovnik was heavily shelled in 1991 and the siege is living memory for many residents. The Fort Imperial museum on Srđ tells this story with dignity. Approach it with respect.

culturalTips.title: Beyond Game of Thrones
culturalTips.text: Dubrovnik was a powerful independent republic for centuries before it became a filming location. Its history of diplomacy, maritime trade, and literary culture is far richer than its TV fame.

culturalTips.title: Photography Etiquette
culturalTips.text: The Old Town is one of the most photographed cities in the world, but respect residents and their laundry. Do not enter private courtyards for photos. Drones are prohibited in the Old Town.

culturalTips.title: Learn Basic Croatian
culturalTips.text: Bok (hello), hvala (thank you), molim (please), and dobar dan (good day). Dubrovnik is very tourist-friendly but a few Croatian words earn genuine warmth.

culturalTips.title: Visit Off-Peak Hours
culturalTips.text: The Old Town receives up to 10,000 cruise visitors per day in peak season. Visiting early morning and evening lets you experience the city as residents know it, peaceful and beautiful.

culturalTips.title: Explore Beyond the Walls
culturalTips.text: The Old Town is just a fraction of Dubrovnik. Gruž, Lapad, and the surrounding countryside have excellent restaurants, beaches, and local life without the tourist premium.
